### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**10** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via nameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs))_
- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via nameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via nameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via nameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via displayNameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs), nameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/schema-design.mdx`  _(via displayNameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs), nameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via nameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs))_

- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via nameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via nameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via nameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-2.mdx`  _(via nameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via nameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via nameField (literal, a string literal in validateObjectFieldRefs))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bfbbaffc5ac9a97533dd59b3c66a82a739b88409` — the merge of head `8e1531c2dc398ee6687243acc70aacbd21d2cdbc` into base `6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bfbbaffc5ac9a97533dd59b3c66a82a739b88409 && git checkout bfbbaffc5ac9a97533dd59b3c66a82a739b88409
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3 8e1531c2dc398ee6687243acc70aacbd21d2cdbc && git checkout -B drift-repro 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3 && git merge --no-ff 8e1531c2dc398ee6687243acc70aacbd21d2cdbc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8e1531c2dc398ee6687243acc70aacbd21d2cdbc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-field-pointer-unknown-refused.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.ts

Inputs read: card #33101 (body and comments 6852874653, 6880767436, 6880802364, 6880909508, 6881746289), PR #33370 (body, 6 files, net diff against `main` from merge-base `24f2f401`), the check-runs on the head. `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`, the test file and the two changesets are the lane seat's remainder; the changesets are read for ② only.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, narrowed (right).** `object-field-ref-unknown` at `error` now also fires at `objects[N].nameField`, `objects[N].displayNameField` and `objects[N].activityMilestones[M].field`. The rule is already a member of the reference-integrity suite with `runtimeTypes: ['flow', 'object']` (`reference-integrity-suite.ts:464` on `main`), so the narrowing reaches `os build` / `os validate` / `os lint` and every door that calls `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` with `state: 'active'`: the save door (`protocol-save.ts:1713`), the draft promotion (`protocol-history-and-publish.ts:1159`) and the restore door (`refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses`). A draft save returns before any rule runs (`runtime-authoring-gate.ts`, D1). The entry's door list is the true list.
- **No widening anywhere (right).** The diff adds two walks that only push findings; no skip, no export, no schema key, no signature changes. `validate-record-title.ts`, `build-probes.ts`, `object-graph.ts` and `runtime-gate.ts` are untouched, and none of the code the diff cites moved on `main` in the 20 commits since the base.
- **Publish probe receipt (right).** `build-probes.ts:417` calls this rule on the published body, so the receipt reports the new positions with no change there.
- **Differential (right).** A finding located on the written item is never cancelled by its stored self (`addedFindings` reads the stored pass only for findings on another entry), and a sibling's finding is present in the baseline pass and cancels. Both halves of the entry's sentence on stored objects are what the gate does. The new positions resolve against the object's own field map only, so a write of object A cannot mint a finding on object B.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/33101-object-field-pointer-unknown.md`: `@objectstack/lint` minor, `fix(lint)!`, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, the ADR-0087 marker naming the entry id. Matches what the diff publishes: a refusal narrowing with no exported type or signature change.
- `.changeset/33101-object-field-pointer-semantic-entry.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch for the ledger entry alone (no key, no export). Matches.
- Clause-②: no (narrowing) — agreed. The PR body, the changeset and the claim carry the same line.
- Gate verdict for this section is not yet rendered by CI: see the check-run note under ③.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report (6881746289). Nothing to answer.
- Out-of-scope note 1 (`tenancy.tenantField` / `tenancy.organizationField` / `lifecycle.ttl.field` stay unjudged): answered. The module header keeps the deferral in its NOT-owned list with the reason; no card is owed by this PR.
- Out-of-scope note 2 (main moved 20 commits): answered by measurement here. Between `24f2f401` and `main`, none of `validate-object-field-refs.ts`, `object-graph.ts`, `runtime-gate.ts`, `system-fields.ts`, `injected-system-columns.ts`, `display-name.ts`, `audit-writers.ts` changed; two unrelated semantic entries were added or edited.
- File surface: the spec entry was added to the claim by amendment 6880909508 before the report. The diff stays inside the amended surface.
- **Check-runs on the head, as read for this record:** 17 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 17 still in progress (Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Type Check workspace / consumer gates / debt ledger, Lint docs and code guards / repo and tooling gates / query-options erasure). Completed and green include Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint PM dispatch-gates. This record judges the design; the gate families still running had rendered no verdict when it was written, and the seat reads their conclusions before it enqueues.

### ④ Design judgment

**The entry (`18.object-field-pointer-unknown-refused.ts`), sentence by sentence against `main`.**

- `surface`: three keys, the doors and the three CLI commands. Holds (① above). `ObjectExtensionSchema` is strict with no `nameField` or `activityMilestones`, so there is no second authoring position the entry forgets.
- `replacement`, "the name is read as a record key, so a dotted path is one name no field carries". Holds on both readers: `resolveRecordDisplayName` reads `record[field]` (`display-name.ts:262`), `titleFieldOf` and the list read use the pointer the same way, and `matchMilestone` reads `after[m.field]` / `before[m.field]` (`audit-writers.ts:1016`). The rule calls `judge` with `verbatim: true`, and `resolveName` answers `field-unknown` for a dotted name without walking it.
- `replacement`, "or at a column the platform injects on it". Holds: an undotted name goes to `resolveFieldPath`, whose leaf accepts `obj.injected`, built per object from `resolveInjectedSystemColumns` (the plan `applySystemFields` consumes). `owner_id` is absent under `ownership: 'none'`, on `sys_*` and on `managedBy` objects, as at runtime.
- `reason`, "titles every record by its id" and "never transitions, so it never fires". Holds: an explicit pointer wins over the derivation in `resolveDisplayField` with no fallback, and `provisionPrimary` is a no-op on an explicit pointer (designate-only at the registry seam, so no `name` column is synthesized behind a dangling `nameField: 'name'`).
- `reason`, the stored-object sentence. Holds (① differential).
- `acceptanceCriteria`. Holds, with nit 3.

**The implementing file (`validate-object-field-refs.ts`).**

- Alias handling: `nameField` is judged unless it equals `displayNameField`; the alias is always judged. Matches the parse (`normalizeNameFieldAlias` copies the alias only when `nameField` is absent) and reports the card's repro once, at the key the author wrote. All four combinations (either alone, both alike, both different) come out as the header says.
- Milestones: non-record entries and a non-string or empty `field` are skipped; the schema owns those shapes.
- Header claims about the neighbours, read on `main`: `objectTitleCompleteness` grades a pointer to a missing field `synthesized` and `validateRecordTitle` reports only `none`; `validateSemanticRoles` reads the pair only to resolve a title. No rule owned the position. Holds.

**Attempts to break it (false refusals of a valid stack).**

- Injected columns: `id` survives `systemFields: false` and better-auth; audit, tenant and ownership columns follow the per-object plan. The lint has no deployment input, so `organization_id` on a deployment-declared platform-global object is accepted, the non-refusing direction.
- Extension-added fields: the graph is `indexServedObjectGraph`, which folds `objectExtensions` (stack and `packages[]` forms), so on the CLI a pointer at a field a sibling package adds resolves. The door snapshot carries no `objectExtensions`, but an object body cannot declare a `__c` field, a base object is extended and never rewritten by a customer (ADR-0146 D10), and an extension cannot carry either key, so no writable body reaches the door naming an extension-only field through its own title pointer or milestone. The channel is the one `highlightFields` has had since #15254; this diff does not open a new one.
- Studio GET, edit, PUT: the read exit stamps a designate-only `nameField` derived from a field of the served body (the registry withholds the stamp when it would name an `extend`-folded field), so a round-tripped body resolves whether or not the write-side strip has run.
- Objects with no readable field map (`external`, introspected) and objects outside the stack are not judged, as at every other position of the rule.
- Packaged versus authored: the CLI judges every object of the stack alike; at the door only the written item is charged. Dev corpus sweep (137 objects, HotCRM by source text) reports 0 findings; nothing read here contradicts it.

No must-fix and no should-fix found.

**Findings.**

1. **nit** — entry `replacement` (and the changeset's Now bullet) lists the injected columns as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `owner_id`, `organization_id`; the rule also accepts `created_by`, `updated_by`, `owning_business_unit_id` (owned and business-unit tiers) and `queue` (owned objects). The omission is in the accepting direction, so nobody is wrongly refused; a reader could take the list as closed. Prose-face fix ("such as") or accepted deviation.
2. **nit** — a dangling `displayNameField` beside a valid, different `nameField` is refused, although every reader takes `nameField ?? displayNameField` and never reads the alias there, so the cost the entry's `reason` states (records titled by id) does not occur in that one case. The refusal itself is inside the entry's `surface` and the #19332 ruling (a misspelling is refused loudly); only the stated cost overreaches. Accepted deviation.
3. **nit** — `acceptanceCriteria`: the `PUT ...?mode=draft` half answers 200 whatever the pointers name (a draft save is never gated), so only the `publish-drafts` half proves anything. Prose-face fix or accepted deviation.
4. **nit** — `TITLE_POINTER_PRESCRIPTION` says "this field of the object" and does not mention an injected column, where the milestone hint and `os explain` do. Wording only; a fix moves the head, so it is a follow-up or an accepted deviation.

**VERDICT: PASS**
